[Highlight start] Alcohol can trigger **tachycardia** —a resting heart rate over 100 beats per minute—both while drinking and hours afterward [Highlight end] . Studies show that higher alcohol intake increases heart rate and raises the risk of atrial arrhythmias, even in people without prior heart disease.⁠National Institutes of Health (NIH) | (.gov) +4[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXbI0t_f3r_GXpTOViHioASuvLOI__NUCvIU06L1i2zEsm--DzVFPrWvxU96bqjilGP6vfGJDVLV6sSexa06y1RmTFIO5ElYvqY970-z0G6RD8yoQg6xLRkJ5WUngMikra52Mr7-G8OA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF1_scVSiMdjkjJgIB_XJqCqwN97Okj-Xa0prKESedumWNxq61gMenvMG9HF2W1O4SDTdCTWHyhWDYd4PST8qrB5gu4Pp9XiH2iqm8_JBmYjtEBv4bOtE_RVmImRc-_hnMhOCQ97hRaprV7Avt1joysh8BAHUw_hMRVL29Ng)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmQEBxCJF14Qg5QUARoEacTXoGEsVEP8r3qZDv0pdj60bd7LyhoD3MfXNl74PNSfdjd4dX9ufgcjYiVdDwq_ZpdXdoHH2Zc3rhN-cBGiLIuAxqmBPdfo4BRb-quZHvz7xPSI5p_cRX6Wuee3u1Brm2SNMlvT7HJXP0Q5IfCHQGc_Mck4-AB-UfEnQD5komzHKr1qIg3lR1E0Elmg)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXHwB94S0NGMjuUvpxXQ_nAnVqoBpC6g-wp8wjdtfKLPYvjuJP5ADUfA9_0IXceVGzIphosaCb9kbvgHmOeYO2bCRGhxLe1mEx0MYAf-Fcaqlp-z8Ev27QyndM75AK5rWr)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESwAEBxCJF15rthS-4fxr83SaiOeCWvvNy6IGRoB2hHwm7thyHIoXIyRzsOnl-WD3-7O4c89uwaFsjffAKERMN2WFVqMGSMDPuk166-CIrF6diRGbojOprwJgMZ2goOqjTEQhqHbhpOVJcsfT8O9JfiSd34CwnH4c07w8rz1snoVwAbQvpbJrcBn6TRkFfqMFLePIecHu34zS9ER54_-ZFYLSN-_MqileJoqdn6wrLt9VHJFk3wDBDnOyRKkbCMd1sJJY)

### Why Alcohol Causes a Fast Heart Rate

- **Nervous system shifts:** Alcohol stimulates stress hormones (like adrenaline) and reduces calming parasympathetic activity, pushing the heart to beat faster.⁠Ovid  +2[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESzAEBxCJF17xryfqaI-PAI-F_pP9M8Dr_pm59QnlaqKiK6Dj49Fhwx1pyCG_7S9xNTo82UfpoSWeD-HZgiHzeyEI1NXGfzICxf13GpL2g0u3gnsYFTsKFYwImpilLdrZTNL1_DZy118tIzaJHVxZUq9W5UGsJ43UqzjW7XUlLENhrN5ALBe79rNH_z8MMnuDDDQYcFX3iAxpzc5IWM1TdUqal8kv5z6aW6ch6xD5kv49YPjt8e9Z2CaLtrWQw_9cvkFvSRnPlCVRa_qDCx5g)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmQEBxCJF14Qg5QUARoEacTXoGEsVEP8r3qZDv0pdj60bd7LyhoD3MfXNl74PNSfdjd4dX9ufgcjYiVdDwq_ZpdXdoHH2Zc3rhN-cBGiLIuAxqmBPdfo4BRb-quZHvz7xPSI5p_cRX6Wuee3u1Brm2SNMlvT7HJXP0Q5IfCHQGc_Mck4-AB-UfEnQD5komzHKr1qIg3lR1E0Elmg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXLSilbrgxY30ED38HTSohlxdTXpaZ1QY3qUb4fb4ovvFcCYA3YTGSLgKQA5tuPIv015Re_abtmaKMR0fgbxrAll1Mby68KEtMv495m1AR6f-CJvcLIfxup9dV38eBHaZ0CcgqlUZttw)
- **Dehydration:** Alcohol acts as a diuretic, lowering fluid volume and forcing the heart to pump faster to maintain circulation.⁠Alina Lodge[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmQEBxCJF14Qg5QUARoEacTXoGEsVEP8r3qZDv0pdj60bd7LyhoD3MfXNl74PNSfdjd4dX9ufgcjYiVdDwq_ZpdXdoHH2Zc3rhN-cBGiLIuAxqmBPdfo4BRb-quZHvz7xPSI5p_cRX6Wuee3u1Brm2SNMlvT7HJXP0Q5IfCHQGc_Mck4-AB-UfEnQD5komzHKr1qIg3lR1E0Elmg)
- **Rebound and withdrawal:** As alcohol wears off, nervous system rebound ("hangxiety") can speed up your pulse. In people who drink heavily or daily, a racing heart 6 to 24 hours after the last drink can be an early sign of alcohol withdrawal.⁠Alina Lodge[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmQEBxCJF14Qg5QUARoEacTXoGEsVEP8r3qZDv0pdj60bd7LyhoD3MfXNl74PNSfdjd4dX9ufgcjYiVdDwq_ZpdXdoHH2Zc3rhN-cBGiLIuAxqmBPdfo4BRb-quZHvz7xPSI5p_cRX6Wuee3u1Brm2SNMlvT7HJXP0Q5IfCHQGc_Mck4-AB-UfEnQD5komzHKr1qIg3lR1E0Elmg)
- **Holiday heart syndrome:** Binge or heavy drinking can trigger irregular rhythms—most commonly atrial fibrillation (AFib)—that feel like rapid or fluttering heartbeats.⁠Ovid  +2[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESzAEBxCJF17xryfqaI-PAI-F_pP9M8Dr_pm59QnlaqKiK6Dj49Fhwx1pyCG_7S9xNTo82UfpoSWeD-HZgiHzeyEI1NXGfzICxf13GpL2g0u3gnsYFTsKFYwImpilLdrZTNL1_DZy118tIzaJHVxZUq9W5UGsJ43UqzjW7XUlLENhrN5ALBe79rNH_z8MMnuDDDQYcFX3iAxpzc5IWM1TdUqal8kv5z6aW6ch6xD5kv49YPjt8e9Z2CaLtrWQw_9cvkFvSRnPlCVRa_qDCx5g)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmQEBxCJF14Qg5QUARoEacTXoGEsVEP8r3qZDv0pdj60bd7LyhoD3MfXNl74PNSfdjd4dX9ufgcjYiVdDwq_ZpdXdoHH2Zc3rhN-cBGiLIuAxqmBPdfo4BRb-quZHvz7xPSI5p_cRX6Wuee3u1Brm2SNMlvT7HJXP0Q5IfCHQGc_Mck4-AB-UfEnQD5komzHKr1qIg3lR1E0Elmg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXX3zzN-P0JbM7MIFMU-nHy2fXV9XkzEODX9kufrXPZGk0j9kV95X6Cvh2HqvlYXcYDOruUV_Bn66lSCla1IltQuoJRDWM0Mzltv-prxq8I2wAqKPHy4yIqaj8NB1aqCXmm)

### What to Expect and When to Seek Care

- **Mild, temporary episodes:** A fast heart rate after light to moderate drinking often settles within several hours as alcohol clears and you rehydrate. You can explore research on acute alcohol intake and heart rhythms in [Alcohol consumption, sinus tachycardia, and cardiac arrhythmias](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXbI0t_f3r_GXpTOViHioASuvLOI__NUCvIU06L1i2zEsm--DzVFPrWvxU96bqjilGP6vfGJDVLV6sSexa06y1RmTFIO5ElYvqY970-z0G6RD8yoQg6xLRkJ5WUngMikra52Mr7-G8OA).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmQEBxCJF14Qg5QUARoEacTXoGEsVEP8r3qZDv0pdj60bd7LyhoD3MfXNl74PNSfdjd4dX9ufgcjYiVdDwq_ZpdXdoHH2Zc3rhN-cBGiLIuAxqmBPdfo4BRb-quZHvz7xPSI5p_cRX6Wuee3u1Brm2SNMlvT7HJXP0Q5IfCHQGc_Mck4-AB-UfEnQD5komzHKr1qIg3lR1E0Elmg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXbI0t_f3r_GXpTOViHioASuvLOI__NUCvIU06L1i2zEsm--DzVFPrWvxU96bqjilGP6vfGJDVLV6sSexa06y1RmTFIO5ElYvqY970-z0G6RD8yoQg6xLRkJ5WUngMikra52Mr7-G8OA)
- **When to see a doctor:** Get evaluated if palpitations keep coming back, if you suspect alcohol withdrawal, or if you have trouble cutting back. For broader heart effects, see [Cleveland Clinic](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF1_scVSiMdjkjJgIB_XJqCqwN97Okj-Xa0prKESedumWNxq61gMenvMG9HF2W1O4SDTdCTWHyhWDYd4PST8qrB5gu4Pp9XiH2iqm8_JBmYjtEBv4bOtE_RVmImRc-_hnMhOCQ97hRaprV7Avt1joysh8BAHUw_hMRVL29Ng).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmQEBxCJF14Qg5QUARoEacTXoGEsVEP8r3qZDv0pdj60bd7LyhoD3MfXNl74PNSfdjd4dX9ufgcjYiVdDwq_ZpdXdoHH2Zc3rhN-cBGiLIuAxqmBPdfo4BRb-quZHvz7xPSI5p_cRX6Wuee3u1Brm2SNMlvT7HJXP0Q5IfCHQGc_Mck4-AB-UfEnQD5komzHKr1qIg3lR1E0Elmg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF1_scVSiMdjkjJgIB_XJqCqwN97Okj-Xa0prKESedumWNxq61gMenvMG9HF2W1O4SDTdCTWHyhWDYd4PST8qrB5gu4Pp9XiH2iqm8_JBmYjtEBv4bOtE_RVmImRc-_hnMhOCQ97hRaprV7Avt1joysh8BAHUw_hMRVL29Ng)
- **Emergency signs:** Seek emergency care right away for chest pain, severe shortness of breath, fainting, confusion, seizures, or a fast/irregular heartbeat that will not settle.⁠Alina Lodge[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmQEBxCJF14Qg5QUARoEacTXoGEsVEP8r3qZDv0pdj60bd7LyhoD3MfXNl74PNSfdjd4dX9ufgcjYiVdDwq_ZpdXdoHH2Zc3rhN-cBGiLIuAxqmBPdfo4BRb-quZHvz7xPSI5p_cRX6Wuee3u1Brm2SNMlvT7HJXP0Q5IfCHQGc_Mck4-AB-UfEnQD5komzHKr1qIg3lR1E0Elmg)

Are you asking for yourself or someone else, and what are you hoping to focus on—such as **immediate relief tips**, **possible causes like withdrawal or AFib** , or **long-term heart risks** ? Sharing **when the fast heart rate happens** (during drinking, the next morning, or after stopping) and **any other symptoms** can also help me tailor this information.

items.title: Why Alcohol Causes a Fast Heart Rate
items.text: Nervous system shifts: Alcohol stimulates stress hormones (like adrenaline) and reduces calming parasympathetic activity, pushing the heart to beat faster. Dehydration: Alcohol acts as a diuretic, lowering fluid volume and forcing the heart to pump faster to maintain circulation. Rebound and withdrawal: As alcohol wears off, nervous system rebound ("hangxiety") can speed up your pulse. In people who drink heavily or daily, a racing heart 6 to 24 hours after the last drink can be an early sign of alcohol withdrawal. Holiday heart syndrome: Binge or heavy drinking can trigger irregular rhythms—most commonly atrial fibrillation (AFib)—that feel like rapid or fluttering heartbeats.

- **Emergency signs:** Seek emergency care right away for chest pain, severe shortness of breath, fainting, confusion, seizures, or a fast/irregular heartbeat that will not settle.⁠Alina Lodge[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmQEBxCJF14Qg5QUARoEacTXoGEsVEP8r3qZDv0pdj60bd7LyhoD3MfXNl74PNSfdjd4dX9ufgcjYiVdDwq_ZpdXdoHH2Zc3rhN-cBGiLIuAxqmBPdfo4BRb-quZHvz7xPSI5p_cRX6Wuee3u1Brm2SNMlvT7HJXP0Q5IfCHQGc_Mck4-AB-UfEnQD5komzHKr1qIg3lR1E0Elmg)
